findings.note: The CBS preview from Oct 20 says San Jose is playing the second night of a back-to-back after losing 3-1 in Toronto Monday. It also says Montreal has taken three of its past four games in extra time, Caufield scored the OT winner and Fowler made 23 saves. Tonight's goalie isn't confirmed.

CBS shows the records are close, Montreal at 4-3-1 and San Jose at 4-4-1, which makes a big favorite price questionable. CBS lists Montreal at -207, close to the -205 offered. Montreal's last three wins came in a shootout, a shootout and overtime, and it lost 5-4 in its last road game.

Montreal practiced in Brossard on Oct 19. This is its last home game before a four-game road trip, and Reinbacher was recalled from Laval earlier. The snippet I could see didn't include any injury details or tonight's starting goalie.

ESPN's preview shows Toronto at 3.20 GF/G and 3.20 GA/G with a 28.6% power play, and Columbus allowing 3.29 GA/G with a 68.0% penalty kill. CBJ's Talbot is at .873 and Toronto's listed goalies are at .902 and .875, all of which leans toward more goals.

Toronto hosted San Jose on Mon Oct 19, so this is the second game of a back-to-back. A backup goalie is possible, but no confirmed starter for either team turned up, and Covers lists the Over at 5-0 in Toronto's last five third-games-in-four-days.

Covers had no expert or computer picks posted, and its public consensus on the 6.5 total was split 55% Over and 45% Under. Its trends cut both ways: Toronto's Over is 5-1 in its last 6, while CBJ's Under is 5-1 as a home favorite and CBJ have gone Over only 9 times in their last 25.
Hedman was healthy and active on Oct. 15, scoring the overtime winner against Seattle. It was his first goal since Feb. 28, and his coach said it should build his confidence after a long road back.

In the Oct. 1 opener's projected lineup, Hedman was on the second pair with Charle-Edouard D'Astous, behind McDonagh-Cernak. That could mean less ice time or power-play work than in his peak years. This is old lineup info and wasn't confirmed for Oct. 20.

Hedman returned Oct. 1 after missing the end of last season and the playoffs for mental health, plus earlier elbow surgery. He is nearly 36 and dropped weight to adjust to aging, so how well he'll hold up and produce is still unclear.

RotoWire's Oct 18, 2026 update says Theodore has only two assists (plus two goals and 20 shots) in 10 games this season, and his goal against the Penguins ended a seven-game point drought, so his early assist rate is low.

A preseason RotoWire note calls Theodore Vegas's top blueliner, but only narrowly ahead of Rasmus Andersson and Noah Hanifin. It expects him to get first shot at the top power-play unit and notes he managed just 39 points in 70 games last season.

RotoWire note from about 2 days ago: Theodore scored in a 6-2 win over Pittsburgh to end a seven-game scoring drought, leaving him with 2 goals and 2 assists in 10 games. That mix of a recent point and a long dry spell cuts both ways for this Over.

Preseason note: Theodore is only narrowly Vegas's top defenseman, with Rasmus Andersson and Noah Hanifin close behind. He should get first shot at the top power-play unit unless Vegas uses five forwards, and he's coming off a 39-point season, his weakest in years.

Older 2025-26 notes: in an October 2025 game against Tampa Bay, Theodore had an assist but mostly played a shutdown role. Early that season he was off the top power-play unit until Mark Stone got hurt, which shows his power-play role can depend on lineup choices.

Oct 13, 2026: Garland was a game-time decision with an illness. Through four games he had no points, one shot on goal and 12:25 of ice time per game. Luca Del Bel Belluz was named as the replacement if he couldn't play.

Oct 13, 2026: After warmups, Garland was expected to play against Florida. RotoWire said he should get solid second-line minutes if fully healthy, which could mean more ice time than his early-season average. He still had no points through five games. No report found on his status for this game.

March 2026: Garland averaged about 20 goals and 49 points per 82 games over his career. After the trade he scored twice in back-to-back games while playing with Monahan and K. Johnson. That history means a bounce back from his slow start is a real risk to the Under.
